author: Jobe Morrison
title: Reasonable or Overreaction? 3 Bears Takes After Week 5 Loss to Packers - NewsBreak
text:
By Jobe Morrison ,
10 days ago
The Chicago Bears suffered a brutal 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5 , missing an opportunity to seize control of the NFC North race and build momentum in one of the NFL’s biggest rivalries. Instead, Chicago struggled on both sides of the ball, raising questions about its quarterback situation, defensive consistency, and ability to compete for another division title.
Following a loss like this, frustration is understandable, but not every reaction deserves the same level of concern. Are the Bears facing legitimate problems that could derail their season, or are fans overreacting to one ugly performance?
Let’s examine three knee-jerk Bears takes following the Week 5 defeat and determine whether each reaction is reasonable or an overreaction.
Bears Are in Trouble at Quarterback if Caleb Williams Doesn’t Return Soon Jan 18, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) warms up while quarterback Tyson Bagent (17) looks on before an NFC Divisional Round game against the Los Angeles Rams at Soldier Field. David Banks-Imagn Images
Tyson Bagent was awful on Sunday. In a game where he needed to be at his best, he couldn’t even manage the game effectively. Two turnovers, two sacks, and just four yards per attempt made for a putrid performance. The Bears had an opportunity to take control of their rivalry and send a statement. Instead, they failed to deliver.
The easy answer is to call for Case Keenum , but he wasn’t exactly stellar, even with the game largely out of reach. He committed two turnovers and couldn’t lead a scoring drive. If Williams misses Week 6, the Bears need to turn to Keenum, but the outlook remains far from encouraging. Chicago needs The Ice Man back as soon as possible.
Verdict: 100% Reasonable Reaction
The Bears’ Defense Are Pretenders Chicago Bears linebacker Devin Bush (12) fights through a block by Green Bay Packers guard Sean Rhyan (75) in pursuit of running back Marshawn Lloyd (32) on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7.
Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Analytically, the Bears still have a very good defense . However, they allowed 31 points and more than 400 yards on Sunday, bringing their hot streak to a brutal halt at Lambeau Field. Still, until these struggles become a trend, I disagree with the notion that this defense is a pretender. The unit has played very well for much of the season, and it certainly didn’t help that the offense struggled to score and protect the football.
The sky isn’t falling, and this defense still has plenty of playmakers. That said, the cornerbacks must perform better. Chicago allowed too many big plays in both Week 1 and Week 5. That simply cannot continue, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will expect his players to respond when they take the field Sunday.
Verdict: Overreaction
The Bears Are Losing the Early NFC North Race Oct 11, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur and Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson shake hands following the game at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN imagesMandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images
This is a harsh reality. After losing to the Vikings in Week 2 and the Packers in Week 5, the Bears are now 0-2 in divisional play. They have four division games remaining, and in a league where divisional records can determine playoff positioning, Chicago has put itself behind the eight ball early.
The Bears entered the season looking to defend their NFC North title. Although there is still plenty of football to play, fans have legitimate reasons to worry about the team’s slow start within the division. Chicago will need to string together divisional wins to keep pace with its rivals and put itself in a strong position for another playoff run.
Verdict: Reasonable Reaction
summary: The Chicago Bears suffered a brutal 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5 , missing an opportunity to seize control of the NFC North race and build momentum in one of the NFL’s biggest rivalries. Instead, Chicago struggled on both sides of the ball, raising questions about its quarterback situation, defensive consistency, and ability to compete for another division title.
